title: A Typewriter for the Regiment
premise: In 1911 in the river town of Vellmark, Quentin Vasquez cuts type in her father's print shop, where the town's census ledger — every family name, every debt, every secret — is being reset in metal. When the army requisitions the town and seizes the ledger to build its lists of loyalists and enemies, Quentin discovers the name of Tomas Ilves, the boy who taught her the alphabet and who is now declared an enemy of the state. Bound by a peacetime promise that she would always cut his name true, she begins forging the ledger's metal type by night, altering names and smuggling proofs through the occupied streets before the river ice breaks and the army ships its lists downstream. The story ends at the ice-break, when Quentin delivers the true ledger — hidden in a crate of type — to the magistrate's ruined court, forcing the occupying colonel to choose between the law he carries and the record he cannot rewrite, and Quentin claims the print shop, and the town's memory, as her own inheritance.
about_author: Oscar Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former typesetter who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing presses in river towns along the old imperial frontier. A Typewriter for the Regiment is the second novel in a planned trilogy about print, power, and the people who keep the record.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Quentin Vasquez's POV. In her father's print shop, Quentin cuts type and measures her life in what can be lifted with two hands: a chase, a forme, a name. Her father's hands are failing, and the ledger of the town waits to be reset. Emotional beat: quiet pride shadowed by the fear of inheriting a trade with no future.

chapters.title: Names in Metal
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She begins setting the census ledger and finds Tomas Ilves's name among the entries — the boy who left for the capital years ago and never wrote. A memory of their childhood promise surfaces. Emotional beat: longing and the first ache of a debt unpaid.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Warrant
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Soldiers march into Vellmark at dawn; a requisition order nails the print shop shut for army use. Colonel Brandt arrives courteous and cold, claiming the ledger for the regiment's loyalty lists. Emotional beat: the floor dropping out of an ordinary life.

chapters.title: What the Army Cannot Read
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, working under occupation. The soldiers use the presses for proclamations but cannot sort the ledger's type; Quentin becomes indispensable and quietly learns what the lists will decide — who keeps their homes. Emotional beat: the dangerous comfort of being useful to your captors.

chapters.title: A Proof in the Snow
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She pulls an illegal proof of the loyalty list at night and finds Tomas Ilves declared an enemy, his family's house marked for seizure. The promise she made in peacetime turns from memory into obligation. Emotional beat: resolve crystallizing into fear.

chapters.title: The Widow Ilves
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She visits Tomas's mother, who has stopped speaking, and finds the old woman hiding letters from Tomas — letters that mention a typewriter he sent ahead, stored in the print shop's cellar. Emotional beat: grief met with the stubbornness of the living.

chapters.title: Type in the Cellar
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. She uncovers the crate: not just a machine but Tomas's own cast type and a half-written manuscript naming corrupt officers. She realizes the ledger can be altered — and that she is the only person alive with the hands to do it. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration in equal measure.

chapters.title: Apprentice to No One
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. By night she begins resetting names in the ledger's plates, learning forgery of the state one character at a time. A near-discovery by a sentry forces her to invent a system of signals with her father, who has guessed everything. Emotional beat: father and daughter becoming conspirators without saying so.

chapters.title: The Printer's Hands
chapters.summary: Father's POV, the novel's only departure from Quentin. Dying slowly, he reflects on a life spent setting other people's truths and teaches Quentin the final trick of the trade: how to make a lie that will survive a magnifying glass. Emotional beat: inheritance passing not as property but as craft.

chapters.title: Ice on the River
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The river freezes solid, halting the army's shipments — and the deadline for the lists. Brandt announces the ice-break will carry everything downstream at once. Quentin has weeks, not months. Emotional beat: time becoming an antagonist.

chapters.title: An Ally in Uniform
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. A young clerk, Sergeant Mirele, catches her altering a plate — and instead of reporting her, asks her to add his sister's name to the safe list. The conspiracy grows a second pair of hands. Emotional beat: trust as a calculated gamble that feels like relief.

chapters.title: The Proclamation Job
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The army orders ten thousand copies of an execution decree; Quentin must print it with her own hands. She complies — and hides Tomas's manuscript pages in the wastepaper bundle bound for the magistrate's clerk. Emotional beat: complicity's bitter taste, and the first act of open defiance.

chapters.title: What Tomas Sent
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV, interleaved with Tomas's manuscript. His pages reveal why he fled: he witnessed the massacre the ledger's original entries were doctored to conceal. The ledger isn't just names — it's the state's alibi. Emotional beat: the promise expanding from one name to a whole town's truth.

chapters.title: Brandt's Dinner
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. The colonel invites her to dine, praising her type-cutting, and lets slip that he knows a forgery exists — he simply cannot find it. Quentin realizes he is hunting her with courtesy. Emotional beat: the predator's patience, and her own mask holding by a thread.

chapters.title: Mirele's Choice
chapters.summary: Mirele's POV. Interrogated about the missing proofs, Mirele must decide between confession and complicity; he burns his sister's file and lies to Brandt's face for the first time in his career. Emotional beat: a good soldier discovering his conscience has a cost.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Soldiers tear apart the print shop searching for the forged plates. Quentin's father, too weak to stand, sits at the press and prints army proclamations through the entire raid, daring them to stop the work they ordered. Emotional beat: defiance as endurance; the plates survive in the one place they never check.

chapters.title: The Father's Last Forme
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Her father dies at dawn, having locked the true ledger inside the forme of tomorrow's official proclamation. The army will print its own lies with the truth bolted beneath them. Emotional beat: grief fused with a terrible, perfect plan.

chapters.title: Before the Ice Breaks
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. On the last night of winter, Quentin and Mirele load the crate — ledger, type, Tomas's manuscript — onto a sledge. Brandt's men watch the river. The ice groans. Emotional beat: held breath; the point of no return crossed in silence.

chapters.title: The Ice-Break
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. As the river cracks and the army's barge loads, Quentin triggers the press run: every proclamation in town comes off the press with the true ledger's page showing through, pasted to walls in the melting snow. The town reads its own stolen record aloud. Emotional beat: catharsis — the secret becoming a chorus.

chapters.title: The Colonel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV. Confronted with the true record and a town that has all read it, Brandt must choose: massacre a literate town and answer to his own superiors, or let the ledger stand and fall with it. He signs the withdrawal order. Emotional beat: the banality of a villain's retreat.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Bench
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. In the ruined courthouse, Quentin delivers the crate — ledger, type, manuscript — to the returning magistrate, and Tomas Ilves walks in behind him, alive, having followed his own manuscript home. The promise is kept; the debt is paid. Emotional beat: reunion without romance, gratitude without erasure of cost.

chapters.title: A Type of Her Own
chapters.summary: Quentin's POV. Spring. Quentin reopens the print shop under her own name, casting new type — her own designs — and setting the first page of the town's corrected history. Mirele stays as her apprentice; Tomas returns to the capital as a witness. Emotional beat: belonging earned, inheritance claimed, the record finally hers to keep.
